mark_breakdown.desc: Apply $f^{-1}$ to both sides of $(f \circ g)(x) = 2x - 1$

subparts.solution:
$f$ is $y = \sqrt[3]{x}$
$\therefore f^{-1}$ is $x = \sqrt[3]{y} \implies y = x^3$
$\therefore f^{-1}(x) = x^3$
If $(f \circ g)(x) = 2x - 1$,
then $f^{-1}((f \circ g)(x)) = f^{-1}(2x - 1)$
$\therefore (f^{-1} \circ f)(g(x)) = (2x - 1)^3$
$\therefore g(x) = (2x - 1)^3$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To solve for the inner function $g(x)$ in $f(g(x)) = h(x)$, apply $f^{-1}$ to both sides: $g(x) = f^{-1}(h(x))$.
step_by_step: Find $f^{-1}(x)$: for $y = \sqrt[3]{x}$, swap variables to get $x = \sqrt[3]{y} \implies y = x^3$, so $f^{-1}(x) = x^3$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Applying $f$ instead of $f^{-1}$ or cubing individual terms inside the bracket.

mark_breakdown.desc: Apply $f^{-1}$ to the input of $(g \circ f)(x)$

subparts.solution:
If $(g \circ f)(x) = 2x - 1$,
then $(g \circ f)(f^{-1}(x)) = 2f^{-1}(x) - 1$
$\therefore g((f \circ f^{-1})(x)) = 2x^3 - 1$
$\therefore g(x) = 2x^3 - 1$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To find the outer function $g(x)$ given $g(f(x)) = h(x)$, replace $x$ by $f^{-1}(x)$ so that $g(f(f^{-1}(x))) = g(x) = h(f^{-1}(x))$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing the order of operations between $2x^3 - 1$ and $(2x-1)^3$.
